answer: The main driver is humid summer weather, not the catalyst lot. Weekly mean humidity jumps from ~50-58% to ~70-87% around week 14, and residual metal (about 3.1 to 3.7-4.4 wt% for R1-R3) and oxidation onset (about 590 to 570-550 C) shift at the same time. Residual metal vs humidity rises above ~65% RH (about 3 wt% to 5-6 at 95%+) and oxidation onset falls above ~65% RH (about 595 to 550 C), with the same curve for every reactor and every lot (FC-2602..2608), so late lots look worse only because they ran in humid weeks. Run hours (가동시간) show no clear effect. Separate additive factor: R4 sits about 1.2 wt% higher residual metal and about 10-15 C lower onset than R1-R3 at all humidities. Within each lot residual metal also saws up over its use period, but each new lot resets low, so no lot-specific jump. Not formally ruled out: lot x season confound (lots are sequential), no numeric regression done.
assistant_friction: Turn 1 put residual metal (wt%) and onset (C) on one shared axis, making it unreadable, and ignored the 'by reactor' request; fixed by asking one variable per plot. No numeric correlation or regression output, so effect sizes are eyeballed from scatters.
